items.prompt: Given an m × n grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return how many islands there are. Land cells connect horizontally and vertically.
items.why: Connected regions of equal cells in a grid → scan every cell and flood each new region once (islands). Nothing is un-marked (not backtracking), and moves aren't one-directional (not DP).

items.prompt: Given a grid of letters and a word, return true if the word can be spelled by moving between horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, using each cell at most once in the word.
items.why: 'Each cell at most once per path' means you must un-mark a cell when you back out, because another path may need it → backtracking. A flood fill marks cells for good.

items.prompt: A robot starts in the top-left of a grid with some blocked cells and may only move right or down. Count the different routes to the bottom-right.
items.why: Moves only go right/down, so there are no cycles, and each cell's count is top + left → DP on the grid. Enumerating routes by backtracking is exponential, and a flood fill can't count paths.

items.prompt: Given an image as a 2-D array of colours, a starting pixel and a new colour, repaint the starting pixel and every pixel connected to it (4-directionally) that has the same original colour.
items.why: Paint-bucket on a grid → flood fill of one connected region (islands). Recursion is only the tool, and nothing has to be undone.

items.prompt: Each row of a matrix is sorted left to right and each column is sorted top to bottom. Decide whether a target value is in the matrix.
items.why: Sorted rows and columns → discard a row or column per step (staircase from a corner) or binary search. A grid alone isn't the islands pattern: there are no regions, and you never touch most cells.

items.prompt: A board holds 'X' and 'O'. Flip every 'O' to 'X' unless it is connected (4-directionally) to an 'O' on the border of the board.
items.why: Regions that do or don't reach the border → flood from the border cells first and mark what escapes (islands, border variant). Nothing is enumerated or un-done.

items.prompt: Each cell of a grid holds the cost of stepping onto it. You may move in any of the four directions. Find the cheapest total cost from the top-left to the bottom-right.
items.why: Different costs per step → Dijkstra with a min-heap. Plain grid BFS/flood only works when every move costs the same, and four-way moves create cycles, so a right/down DP table doesn't apply.

items.prompt: Given a grid of letters, return true if there is a cycle of length at least 4 made of adjacent cells (up/down/left/right) that all hold the same letter.
items.why: Connected same-value regions in a matrix → DFS over the grid, remembering the parent cell. Reaching a seen cell that isn't your parent closes a loop. No path enumeration (backtracking) and no dependency order (topological sort).
